text:
maria: Heads-up — last hour we had ~14 small GPU pods evicted and rescheduled across us-west1-a/b, looks like the pods keep hopping between a small set of nodes.
ken: saw the spike too, eviction-rate up ~6x at 11:42. Mostly pods with resources: requests: nvidia.com/gpu:1, cpu:200m, mem:512Mi.
maria: logs show scheduler doing prebind serialization for same node annotation repeatedly.
derek: dropping a small scheduler log snippet i pulled: 
```
I0311 11:42:03.123456 1 prebind.go:92] serialized prebind for pod/training-job-xyz -> node/gke-us-west1-a-foo
I0311 11:42:03.223456 1 prebind.go:95] binding failed, requeueing pod/training-job-xyz
```
ken: also noticed warm-pool lease controller holding leases while backing off, so handoff stalls and then the scheduler sees the node as available again briefly.
sre-bot: ALERT: evictions increasing in us-west1 (metric: gpu_evict_count) — 12 pods evicted in 1h, impacting training-jobs namespace.
jia: short hypothesis: our prebind + aggressive binpack heuristic is effectively single-threading small-pod bursts. serialized binds create a tiny window where the node resource view is stale, other decisions assign into same groups -> later reconciliation evicts the earlier ones (pod hopscotch).
ops-lead: can we do a quick mitigation: bump scheduler concurrency or relax the prebind serialization? or reduce warm-pool lease TTL?
derek: quick experiment idea: increase scheduler --concurrent-assigners (or equivalent flag) to 20 and set warm-pool lease TTL -> 5s to reduce handoff holding time.
ken: commands to inspect current leases and pod churn: 
```
kubectl get leases -n kube-system | grep warmpool
# and
kubectl get events -n training-jobs --field-selector reason=Preempted
```
ken: i also pushed a dashboard panel showing "prebind_serialize_count" and "warmpool_lease_hold_time" — currently see spikes aligning with evictions.
maria: operational impact: fragmentation is increasing too — we have many nodes with 1 GPU free scattered across AZ/racks, so any gang job >1 GPU suffers. short-lived small pods amplify fragmentation.
jia: medium-term fixes: 1) coalesce very small workloads into multi-container/sidecar packing jobs, 2) add soft packing preference (podAnnotation => prefer-same-node) for ephemeral workers, 3) improve scheduler snapshot isolation so prebinds don't create stale views.
ops-lead: agreed. immediate plan:
  - ken: canary change to scheduler concurrency in us-west1-a (one AZ) and monitor for 30m
  - derek: adjust warm-pool lease TTL to 5s and watch handoff time
  - jia: add prebind_serialize_count metric + alert (warning threshold if >10/min)
  - maria: run short packing test (10k tiny pods) in staging to quantify fragmentation delta
ken: i'll open the canary PR now and tag you all. if canary improves evictions by >50% we roll plateau.
maria: thanks. ping me if any regressions show up; we should capture cost delta too (wasted GPU-hours). Sync in 30m in #eng-platform to decide roll-forward. :thumbsup:
